column1: # Game profile of JUMP FORCE - Deluxe Edition (Switch, base v0 + update v458752 = 1.08). PEANUTS: Android bring-up, provisional (README.md beside this file)
# Unreal Engine 4 with CRIWARE sound (.awb) and MP4 movies (NintendoSDK_movie), SDK 9.3.1: the sdk and subsdk0 builds are DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT's (010051C0134F8000)
# Provisional game profile (generated by scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py from the survey with dm/games/profile_guess.py, not checked by hand)
# 0100183010F12000, SDK 9, from its survey (survey.md beside the dump)

# Unreal: nninitStartup reserves a 62 GB address region and its FMallocBinned3 takes 37 GB of it, so a 64 GB alias region for the bring-up on the Mac. The rewriter cuts the allocator in any Unreal 4 / 5 main (dm/tools/ue_malloc.py) and gives the region what the alias region has room for (dm/tools/ue_region.py), so an iPhone takes a smaller guest block, as Octopath Traveler 0's profile (docs/reference/memory.md)
# the NPDM declares 40 MB of system resource
# The game engine's Tick (main+0xb4e00, J5 engine) steps the battle (Bandai's CS framework: J5IFSystemInterface::SystemStep(float), main+0x25fe010, builds the CS::CSTickInfo) in fixed
# 1/60 s steps (the constant at main+0x4ca1b3c), as many per frame as the byte at engine+0x3d1 says: 2 in the shipped 30 fps mode (main+0x78150, the game's own 30/60 switch, sets 2
# with a 30 frame limit and 1 with 60). Raising only t.MaxFPS kept two steps a frame: fights ran twice as fast at 60 while menus (Unreal delta time) were right. The plan replaces
# the mode test (main+0xb4f24..0xb4f38) by a load of 60 / fps (vsync_u32, on the plan's data page) into the step count: one step a frame at 60, two at 30, three at 20. With rows
# the host's own t.MaxFPS write is off, so a row writes it (main+0x6a41ce0 +0x10: the game thread's and the render thread's copies). The rows follow the frame limiter's target,
# which the launcher passes (DM_FPS_LIMIT) only with fps_limit: 30 by default, 60 chosen. No 120: one step of 1/120 s a frame (tried 2026-11-27, the data page held 120 / fps and
# 1 / fps as planned) still ran fights twice as fast: their move frames advance once a step whatever its length, so 60 steps a second is the most
# Unreal fills ASTC textures from the CPU in CPU-uncached pools (flags 0xe2) after their first GPU use and never flushes, as in Octopath Traveler: without both keys the GPU keeps
# their first, all-zero blocks (serial 286, 256x256 ASTC 6x6 sRGB: 1849 of 1849 zero on the GPU while guest memory held the data), which Adreno decodes as NaN: the base pass of
# M_MapCommon_Basic1 wrote NaN into scene colour (black floors and streets, black truck), and temporal AA / bloom spread it (black characters, black overlays, white blobs)
# the decoded shader code archives: the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders
